subject: Tufts Park Redesign
overview: The Commission for Persons with Disabilities reviewed redesign plans and accessibility considerations for Tufts Park and received updates on the city's wayfinding study and ADA transition planning. The commission also reviewed outcomes from the recent disability fair and approved its April meeting minutes.

items.title: Introductions and agenda review
items.summary: Commission members and staff introduced themselves and outlined the meeting agenda.

items.title: Tufts Park redesign presentation and feedback
items.summary: City planners and consultants presented early design and survey efforts for Tufts Park, while commissioners provided feedback regarding screen reader accessibility, dog separation, accessible pathways, and restrooms.

items.title: Approval of April minutes
items.summary: The commission approved the meeting minutes from April.

items.title: Disability fair recap
items.summary: Commissioners and staff reviewed the recent disability fair, highlighting positive community attendance and entertainment while noting areas to improve such as signage and water availability.

items.title: Wayfinding study update and grant application
items.summary: Staff reported that feedback from the Institute for Human-Centered Design resulted in adjusted signage designs and noted the city is applying for a state One Stop grant of up to $250,000 for Medford Square rollout.

items.title: Disability Commission ordinance and ADA transition plan updates
items.summary: Staff announced the updated commission ordinance is completing legal review for City Council consideration, and the Institute for Human-Centered Design has begun work on the city's self-evaluation and transition plan.

items.title: Other business and community announcements
items.summary: Commissioners discussed pedestrian signals and voting machine accessibility testing before staff shared announcements for upcoming community events including Pride and Juneteenth.
